items.exampleEn: A full stop shows that a sentence is finished.
items.exampleZh: 句號表示一個句子結束了。

items.exampleEn: Do you need an indefinite article before "water"?
In English, "may" is a modal verb.
items.exampleZh: 在英文裡，「may」是一個情態動詞。

items.exampleEn: "Give up" is a common phrasal verb.
items.exampleZh: 「give up」是一個常見的片語動詞。

items.exampleEn: Primary school lasts six years here.
Use a question mark when you ask something.
Secondary school starts at age twelve here.
items.exampleZh: 這裡的中學從十二歲開始。

items.sentenceEn: Is this a question mark or a full stop?

items.audioEn: After primary school, I went to a secondary school near my house.
items.audioZh: 小學畢業後，我去讀家附近的一所中學。
items.questionZh: 說話者小學畢業後去了哪裡？
options: A school in another city far away.
A music school in the next town.
A high school close to home.

items.sentenceEn: Our town has a new primary school.
items.sentenceZh: 我們鎮上有一所新的小學。

items.sentenceEn: Each phrasal verb has its own meaning.
items.sentenceZh: 每個片語動詞都有自己的意思。

items.stemEn: A sentence like "I am tired" ends with a ____.
items.stemZh: 像「I am tired」這樣的句子要用句號結尾。

items.stemEn: We use a ____ like "should" or "must" to give advice or rules.
items.stemZh: 我們用 should 或 must 這類情態動詞來給建議或定規則。

items.passageEn: Last week, a new sign went up near the primary school in our town, and my class found three mistakes on it. First, the sentence "Please drive slowly" had no full stop. Second, the question "Where is the park" had no question mark. Third, the sign said "a old park." We use "an," not "a," before words that begin with a vowel sound; each of them is an indefinite article. I'm in secondary school now, so my teacher asked me to write a short email to the town office. I used a modal verb to be polite: "Could you please fix the sign?" The office said they would look into it. "Look into" is a phrasal verb that means "check." Two days later, the sign was fixed!
items.passageZh: 上週，我們鎮上的小學附近立了一塊新告示牌，我們班在上面發現了三個錯誤。第一，「Please drive slowly」這句話少了句號。第二，問句「Where is the park」沒有問號。第三，告示牌上寫著「a old park」。在母音開頭的字前面要用「an」，不是「a」；兩者都是不定冠詞。我現在讀中學，所以老師請我寫一封簡短的電子郵件給鎮公所。我用了一個情態動詞讓語氣更有禮貌：「Could you please fix the sign?」鎮公所說他們會 look into 這件事。「look into」是一個片語動詞，意思是「查看」。兩天後，告示牌就改好了！

questions.questionZh: 告示牌上的第一個錯誤是什麼？
作者用什麼讓信的語氣更有禮貌？

resolvedAfterFinalReview.resolution: 改前："Last week, a new sign went up near the primary school in our town, and my class found three mistakes on it. First, the sentence \"Please drive slowly\" had no full stop. Second, the question \"Where is the park\" had no question mark. Third, the sign said \"a old park.\" We use \"an,\" not \"a,\" before words that begin with a vowel sound; both are indefinite articles. I'm in secondary school now, so my teacher asked me to write a short email to the town office. I used a modal verb to be polite: \"Could you please fix the sign?\" The office said they would look into it. \"Look into\" is a phrasal verb that means \"check.\" Two days later, the sign was fixed!"；改後："Last week, a new sign went up near the primary school in our town, and my class found three mistakes on it. First, the sentence \"Please drive slowly\" had no full stop. Second, the question \"Where is the park\" had no question mark. Third, the sign said \"a old park.\" We use \"an,\" not \"a,\" before words that begin with a vowel sound; each of them is an indefinite article. I'm in secondary school now, so my teacher asked me to write a short email to the town office. I used a modal verb to be polite: \"Could you please fix the sign?\" The office said they would look into it. \"Look into\" is a phrasal verb that means \"check.\" Two days later, the sign was fixed!"
